accepted.question_text: Give a mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics by providing an axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems suitable for the foundations of statistical physics, and by developing a rigorous theory of the limiting processes that lead from an atomistic description to the laws of motion of continua.

evidence.quote: H6 concerns the axiomatization of physics. In particular, Hilbert proposed the following two specific problems: (i) the axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems for the foundation of statistical physics and (ii) the rigorous theory of limiting processes "which lead from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua."

accepted.question_text: Determine whether P equals NP, meaning whether every problem whose proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time also has an algorithm that can find a solution in polynomial time.

evidence.quote: • S3 Does P = NP?

accepted.question_text: Extend the mathematical model of general equilibrium theory so that it includes price-adjustment dynamics rather than only equilibrium states.

evidence.quote: • S8 Extend the mathematical model of general equilibrium theory to include price adjustments.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the Navier-Stokes equations in three spatial dimensions always admit a unique smooth solution that exists for all time.

evidence.quote: • S15 Do the Navier-Stokes equations in R3 always have a unique smooth solution that extends for all time?

accepted.question_text: Establish rigorously the existence of quantum Yang-Mills theory together with a mass gap.

evidence.quote: Problem M2 aims to establish the existence of the quantum Yang-Mills theory and a mass gap rigorously, and is truely a problem in mathematical physics.

accepted.question_text: For Newtonian gravitating particles, prove that the set of initial conditions that fail to produce global solutions has measure zero, and determine whether non-collisional singularities can occur in the Newtonian N-body problem.

evidence.quote: • BS1 Existence for Newtonian Gravitating Particles. A: Prove that the set of initial conditions which fails to have global solutions is of measure zero (some mathematicians believe that there may be an open set of initial conditions leading to non-global solutions). B: Existence of non-collisional singularities in the Newtonian N-body problem.

accepted.question_text: Develop a comprehensive theory of the long-time behavior of dynamical systems that also includes a theory for the onset of turbulence and for fully developed turbulence.

evidence.quote: • BS3 Develop a comprehensive theory of the long time behavior of dynamical systems including a theory of the onset of, and of fully developed, turbulence.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the open ergodic-theory questions identified by Simon: determine ergodicity of gases with soft cores, explain approach to equilibrium, and establish asymptotic abelianness for quantum Heisenberg dynamics.

evidence.quote: • BS2 Open Questions in Ergodic Theory. Particular problems include A: Ergodicity of gases with soft cores, B: Approach to equilibrium, and C: Asymptotic Abelianness for the quantum Heisenberg dynamics.

accepted.question_text: Develop a mathematically precise formulation of renormalization-group transformations for ν-dimensional Ising-type systems and, in particular, prove universality by showing that the critical exponents in three-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising models do not depend on anisotropic bond-strength ratios.

evidence.quote: • BS8 Formulation of the Renormalization Group and Proof of Universality. A: Develop a mathematically precise version of the renormalization transformations for ν-dimensional Ising-type systems. B: In particular, show that the critical exponents in the three dimensional Ising models with nearest neighbor coupling but different bond strengths in the three directions are independent of the ratios of these bond strengths.

accepted.question_text: Put quantum field theory on a rigorous mathematical footing by constructing quantum chromodynamics, building a nontrivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theory, proving that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory, or proving that no nontrivial lattice cutoff theory exists.

evidence.quote: • BS14 Quantum field theory remains a basic element of fundamental physics and a continual source of inspiration to mathematicians. A: give a precise mathematical construction of quantum chromodynamics, the model of strong interaction physics. B: Construct any non-trivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theory. C: Prove that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory. D: Prove that a non-trivial lattice cutoff theories theory does not exist.

accepted.question_text: Prove that every Yang-Mills field on the four-sphere S4 is either self-dual or anti-self-dual.

evidence.quote: • Y117 Prove that any YM field on S4 is either self-dual or antiself-dual.

accepted.question_text: Prove that, for a fixed Pontryagin number, the moduli space of self-dual Yang-Mills fields on the four-sphere S4 is connected.

evidence.quote: • Y118 Prove that the moduli space of the self-dual fields on S4 with a fixed Pontryagin number is connected.

accepted.question_text: Determine the range of validity of the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions used to approximate solutions of Einstein's equations.

evidence.quote: • RB20 Determine the range of validity of the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions.

accepted.question_text: Prove rigorously that there exists a limit in which solutions of Einstein's equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

evidence.quote: • RB21 Prove rigorously the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Prove that a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R × M^3.

evidence.quote: • RB32 Prove that a "cosmological spacetime" satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or it splits as R × M3 isometrically (and is thus static).

accepted.question_text: Find an exact solution of Einstein's equations that represents two orbiting bodies, and determine whether the two-body system is unstable in Einstein gravity.

evidence.quote: • RB43 Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations which represents two orbiting bodies. Is the 2-body system unstable in Einstein gravity?

accepted.question_text: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture in general relativity: for generic initial data for the evolution problem, naked singularities should not occur.

evidence.quote: The weak cosmic censorship hypothesis states that: For generic initial data to the evolution problem in GR, there cannot be naked singularities. This is such an open problem that the correct formulation of the statement is not even known. Problem P1: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a three-dimensional compact manifold. Prove that, for generic vacuum initial data on M, the maximal vacuum Cauchy development equals the maximal vacuum extension of M.

evidence.quote: Problem P2: Let M be a 3 dimensional compact manifold. Prove that the maximal vacuum Cauchy development for generic vacuum data sets is equal to the maximal vacuum extension of M.

accepted.question_text: Either prove the Penrose inequality in full generality or produce a counterexample to it.

evidence.quote: Problem P3: Find a proof of the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample in the general case.

accepted.question_text: For collisionless matter models, prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data; also prove existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions such as Bianchi type IX solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov equations, and investigate the large-initial-data regime.

evidence.quote: Problem P4 : Prove the global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data in collisionless matter models. Prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous (such as Bianchi type IX) solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov equations and investigate the large initial data case.

accepted.question_text: Prove nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole under perturbations.

evidence.quote: Problem P5: Prove the stability of the Kerr black hole.

accepted.question_text: Determine when a four-dimensional spacetime can be reconstructed explicitly from its scalar curvature invariants, and identify a minimal set of invariants sufficient for that reconstruction.

evidence.quote: Problem PF1 : Determine when a 4D spacetime can be explicitly constructed from its scalar curvature invariants and determine the minimal set of such invariants.

accepted.question_text: Formulate an appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon in general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem P6: Formulate an appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon.

accepted.question_text: Prove rigorously that test particles of negligible mass move on spacetime geodesics in general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem P7 : Prove that test particles move on spacetime geodesics.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, with weakly turbulent transfer of energy to high frequencies leading to black-hole formation, persists or changes in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse.

evidence.quote: Problem P8: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability in Anti-de Sitter spacetime, which leads to a weakly turbulent mechanism that develops a cascade towards high frequencies leading to black hole formation, behaves differently in more general models than spherically symmetric scalar field collapse.

accepted.question_text: Determine the uniqueness classification of black holes in higher-dimensional spacetimes.

evidence.quote: Problem P9: Determine the uniqueness of black holes in higher dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Determine the stability properties of black holes in higher-dimensional spacetimes.

evidence.quote: Problem P10: Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether singularity-resolution results proved in spatially homogeneous loop quantum gravity or loop quantum cosmology can be extended and proved in more general, less symmetry-reduced settings.

evidence.quote: Problem P11: Can the singularity resolution results obtained in the spatially homogeneous spacetimes in LQG be proven in a more general setting.

accepted.question_text: Prove a cosmic no-hair theorem for generic inhomogeneous spacetimes.

evidence.quote: Problem P12: Prove a cosmic no–hair theorem in generic inhomogeneous spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system is exactly the Mixmaster attractor, rather than merely a subset of it.

evidence.quote: Problem P13: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system coincides with the Mixmaster attractor (as defined in [251] – the Bianchi II variety of [253]) rather than being a subset thereof.

accepted.question_text: Prove the BKL locality conjecture for general inhomogeneous spacetimes approaching a generic spacelike singularity.

evidence.quote: Problem P14: Prove the BKL locality conjecture in the general inhomogeneous context.

accepted.question_text: Prove that spike structures occur near generic cosmological singularities and determine how those spikes affect any eventual proof of generic singularity behavior.

evidence.quote: Problem P15: Prove the existence of spikes and determine their effect on any eventual generic singularity proofs.

accepted.question_text: Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities when general matter fields present in the early universe are included.

evidence.quote: Problem P16: Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities for general matter fields present in the early universe.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity.

evidence.quote: Problem P17: Are isotropic singularities typical in modified theories of gravity.

accepted.question_text: Give a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem PF2 Provide a rigorous mathematical definition for averaging in GR.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether averaging and backreaction can play an important role in cosmology, and in particular identify the largest scale on which matter and geometry can be coarse-grained while the averaged evolution still exactly satisfies Einstein's equations.

evidence.quote: Problem PF3 Can averaging play an important role in cosmology. In particular, what is the largest scale that we can coarse-grain matter and geometry that obeys Einstein’s equations on smaller scales such that the average evolution is still an exact solution of Einstein’s equations.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the black hole information paradox.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF1: Resolve the black hole information paradox.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the cosmological constant problem and the problem of dark energy.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF2: The cosmological constant problem and dark energy.

accepted.question_text: Formulate a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF3: Formulate a fully consistent theory of QG.

accepted.question_text: Determine how generic inflation is for generic initial data.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP1: What is the generality of inflation for generic initial data.

accepted.question_text: Determine the emitted gravitational-wave waveforms for binary black-hole systems with enough accuracy for optimal detection and parameter extraction.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP2: Determine the predictions of emitted waveforms for binary black hole systems for optimal detection and parameter extraction.

accepted.question_text: Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse within general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP3: Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR.
